speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I wish to thank Mdm Speaker, the Prime Minister and Members of the House for your well wishes when I was not well.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Your kindness and encouragement are both humbling and uplifting to me and my family.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Events since then are a stark reminder of how quick and unpredictable change can be.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is an inward-looking mood in several of the most advanced economies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Should this translate into protectionist actions, it will slow global trade and investments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Meanwhile, advances in technology are picking up pace, disrupting traditional businesses and jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But they also present opportunities for countries and people who can learn and adapt quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These deep shifts around the world will create new challenges but also open up new opportunities for many years to come.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must understand these shifts and do our best to adapt and thrive.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is also undergoing a key transition as our economy matures.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With falling birth rates and a rapidly ageing population, labour force growth will eventually fall to zero.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore should develop strong capabilities in our firms and workers, so that they can adapt to the changes in economic structures and technology.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Digitalisation, innovation and highly-skilled workers will enable cities and regions to prosper while staying open and connected to the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, we must forge deep partnerships in our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government's role is not to plan every move, but to forge a common understanding of the changes, and foster partnerships with businesses, unions, firms and workers, with each playing a key role.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to pool our resources and ideas and solve problems together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Such networks of trust will allow us to seize opportunities and respond to unexpected challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Similarly, we need to foster partnerships in the wider society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can maintain a good balance between state action and community initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government can do good in many instances, but so can individual citizens.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When friends, neighbours and fellow citizens come together in support of a cause or one another, we forge deep bonds and grow our social capital.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is critical that we take decisive action to reposition ourselves for the future.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2017 will outline measures for our economy and our society, together with fiscal policies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will take a learning and adaptive approach, try new methods, continue with them when they work well, cut losses when they do not, and draw on feedback and experience to refine and adjust our plans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is similar to the 1.9 % growth achieved in 2015.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is within range, but at the lower end of our potential growth over the medium term.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But this aggregate growth figure belies the uneven performance across sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Sectors, such as electronics, information and communications, and education, health and social services, did well.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some sectors have been harder hit by cyclical weaknesses, including marine and offshore and, to some extent, construction.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Other sectors, like retail, are facing structural shifts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The picture of the labour market is similarly mixed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Sectors such as healthcare and education, offered more jobs, while others shed them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2016, resident employment increased while foreign employment contracted3.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given the uneven performance across different sectors, we need to go beyond general stimulus, and target the specific issues faced by different sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For firms and sectors that are doing well, we must focus on the long term and build on the momentum to seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, firms in the manufacturing sector should adopt advanced manufacturing technologies to build competitive advantage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In last year's Budget, I announced the $450 million National Robotics Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, I will be announcing measures to help firms with good prospects scale up and internationalise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For sectors facing cyclical weaknesses, we have introduced specific support measures like the Bridging Loan for Marine and Offshore Engineering companies, which provides access to working capital to help them bridge short-term cash flow gaps.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will introduce specific measures to address continued cyclical weaknesses in the marine and process sectors, and the construction sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, we deferred foreign worker levy increases in the marine and process sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our construction firms will be able to bid for and participate in these projects, which include the upgrading of community clubs and sports facilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms in sectors that are facing structural shifts will need to dig deep to change their business models to stay viable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, firms and workers in retail will need to embrace digital capabilities to access new markets through online-marketing and e-commerce platforms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will help workers adapt to structural shifts in the economy, especially those who seek to move to a different sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Instead, industry partners can send participants for training and work attachments.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will increase the chances of these workers to find a job in the sector later.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Manpower will elaborate on the initiatives at the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the next two to three years, the different sectors of our economy will be in transition, repositioning themselves for the future economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some firms may need help to manage cost or cash flow.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will continue to receive support from schemes announced previously.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Roughly 70% of this amount will be to small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Special Employment Credit will continue to provide employers with support for the wages of older workers till 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SME Working Capital Loan will continue to be available for the next two years.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is where the Government co-shares 50% of the default risk for loans of up to $300,000 per SME.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There has been good take-up for this scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since its launch in June 2016, the scheme has catalysed more than $700 million of loans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will introduce two more measures to support firms.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, I will enhance the Corporate Income Tax (CIT) Rebate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The rebate will remain at 50% of tax payable.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also extend the CIT rebate for another year to YA2018, at a reduced rate of 20% of tax payable, capped at $10,000.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The enhancement and extension will cost an additional $310 million over YA2017 and YA2018.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will provide more support for firms hiring older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MOM will raise the re-employment age from 65 to 67, with effect from 1 July 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will apply to workers younger than 65 on that day.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To encourage employers to continue hiring workers who are not covered, we will extend the Additional Special Employment Credit till end-2019.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under this scheme, employers will receive wage offsets of up to 3% for workers who earn under $4,000 per month, and who are not covered by the new re-employment age of 67.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taken together with the Special Employment Credit, employers will receive support of up to 11% for the wages of their eligible older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The extension of the Additional Special Employment Credit will benefit about 120,000 workers and 55,000 employers and will cost about $160 million.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This helps to extend the employability of older Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These additional near-term support measures, with the existing Wage Credit Scheme and Special Employment Credit, will give businesses support of over $1.4 billion over the next year.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The measures I have described will help our firms and workers, especially in sectors that are facing cyclical or structural weaknesses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even more important is how we increase our growth in the medium to long term, so as to sustain our potential growth of 2% to 3%.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These measures largely respond to the ideas put forth by the Committee on the Future Economy, or CFE.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The CFE has laid out seven mutually reinforcing strategies to tackle the challenges ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These strategies are not prescriptive blueprints but focus on developing adaptability and resilience.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These qualities will keep Singapore relevant even as the world changes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Emerging economies are now able to produce rather than import higher value components.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is also a growing consumer class in many Asian cities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we stay open and connected, we have to understand our global partners and customers much better and more deeply.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our enterprises and people will need to venture overseas and to immerse themselves in these markets to gain deep insights.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Technology is reshaping businesses, jobs and lifestyles across the world.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must spot the opportunities in the digital economy and make the most of our strengths as a nimble, well-educated, tech-savvy society.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we mature as an economy, we must compete on the quality and novelty of our ideas and our ability to create value.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to build a strong innovation and enterprise engine, to complement our traditional strengths in efficiency and speed.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These moves will entail building capabilities of our enterprises, the capabilities of our people, and bringing all parts together in partnership to act as one agile, adaptable whole.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This, in essence, is the key thrust of the CFE recommendations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our enterprises to stay competitive and grow, they will need to develop deep capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Which capabilities matter − this depends on the industry that the firm is in, and the firm's own stage of growth.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But there are three capabilities that many firms will need in common − being able to use digital technology, embrace innovation and scale up.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Digital technology has a unique potential to transform businesses, large and small, across the economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) will work with SPRING and other sector lead agencies in this effort.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SMEs Go Digital Programme will have three components.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, SMEs will get step-by-step advice on the technologies to use at each stage of their growth through the sectoral Industry Digital Plans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will start with sectors where digital technology can significantly improve productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include retail, food services, wholesale trade, logistics, cleaning and security.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, SMEs will get in-person help at SME Centres and a new SME Technology Hub to be set up by IMDA.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SMEs can approach business advisors at SME Centres for advice on off-the-shelf technology solutions that are pre-approved for funding support or connect to infocommunications and technology (ICT) vendors and consultants.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The more digitally advanced firms can get specialist advice from the SME Technology Hub.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, SMEs that are ready to pilot emerging ICT solutions can receive advice and funding support.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will work with consortiums of large and small firms to help them adopt impactful, interoperable ICT solutions to level up whole sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also strengthen our capabilities in data and cybersecurity.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With increased digitalisation, data will become an important asset for firms, and strong cybersecurity is needed for our networks to function smoothly.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for Communications and Information will elaborate at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second way to strengthen our enterprises is to support firms in their broader efforts to tap on innovation and technology.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With our consistent investments in research and development, we have built up excellent research institutes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We want to help companies better tap on these resources.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) currently works with firms to conduct operation and technology road-mapping to identify how technology can help them innovate and compete.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For companies seeking access to intellectual property (IP), Intellectual Property Intermediary, a SPRING affiliate, matches them with IP that meets their needs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will work with the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS) to analyse and bundle complementary IP from Singapore and overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A*STAR also partners SMEs through the Headstart Programme.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Headstart Programme allows SMEs that co-develop IP with A*STAR to enjoy royalty-free and exclusive licences for 18 months in the first instance.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also support companies in the use of advanced machine tools for prototyping and testing, which may require costly specialised equipment.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A*STAR will provide access to such equipment, user training and advice under a new Tech Access Initiative.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministers for Trade and Industry will elaborate at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third way to strengthen our enterprises is to help them scale up globally.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Singapore-based firms already have a presence in other markets, often with support from International Enterprise (IE) Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Fund will co-invest with Singapore-based firms to help them scale-up and internationalise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: An important opportunity for our companies is the growing market for infrastructure development in emerging economies, especially in Asia.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, there remain gaps in financial markets for project finance in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will enhance its schemes to bridge these gaps, by catalysing private finance and sharing risks with financial institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We set up Clifford Capital in 2012 to finance overseas projects by Singapore companies.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To date, over $2.4 billion have been committed4.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will enhance IE Singapore's Internationalisation Finance Scheme to further support growth in this sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will catalyse private cross-border project financing to smaller Singapore-based infrastructure developers, by co-sharing the default risk of lower quantum non-recourse loans.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also catalyse financing for projects undertaken by large firms in higher-risk developing markets, by providing a share of the needed sovereign risk insurance coverage.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overall, these enhancements will enable more companies to take on more overseas projects.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministers for Trade and Industry will provide more details at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To sum up, these are the measures to help enterprises build capabilities to go international, go digital, and innovate.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Next, I will speak on how we will help our people deepen their capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our people are valued for their skills and adaptability and have enjoyed high employment rates and rising wages.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the pace of change quickens, we will do more to help them stay ahead.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I spoke earlier about how we will support those affected by economic restructuring to reskill to find new jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Global Innovation Alliance will have three programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, the Innovators Academy will enable our tertiary students to build connections and capabilities overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will build on the National University of Singapore Overseas College programme, which connects students to startups overseas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of these students have gone on to start companies or pursue interesting careers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will establish Innovation Launchpads in selected overseas markets.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These create opportunities for our entrepreneurs and business owners to connect with mentors, investors and service providers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, through Welcome Centres, innovative foreign companies can also link up with Singapore partners to co-innovate, test new products in Singapore, and expand in the region.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Global Innovation Alliance is a novel collaboration among our educational institutions, economic agencies and businesses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministers for Trade and Industry will share more details at the COS.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Firms that want to expand overseas need capable leaders who have spent time in these markets, with insights and connections that can help their businesses scale up globally.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative will support companies to groom Singaporean leaders by expanding leadership development initiatives.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes sending promising individuals on specialised courses and overseas postings.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our companies innovate and digitalise, we will help our people acquire and use deep skills, taking the SkillsFuture movement further.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To enhance training and make it more accessible, we will offer more short, modular courses and expand the use of e-learning.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our universities, polytechnics and ITE have started offering such modular courses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Funding support for Singaporeans to take approved courses will continue to be available under SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides learning new skills, our people must also apply and use these skills on their jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This requires employers, trade associations and chambers (TACs), unions and the Government to work together.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we must make sure that skilled workers are matched to where they can best use their skills.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will make the National Jobs Bank more useful for jobseekers and employers, and work with private placement firms to deliver better job matching services for professionals.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, employers, TACs, and unions should play an active role in structuring training for workers.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, SHATEC5 was set up by the Singapore Hotel Association over 30 years ago to provide hands-on training and certified courses.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has since helped to build up a skilled hospitality workforce, with its alumni winning accolades worldwide.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We hope more employers and TACs can do likewise.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Employers and TACs who develop training programmes for their workers and the industry can receive funding support from SkillsFuture Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken about how we will support the development of our enterprises and our people.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond developing individual capabilities, we must also come together in partnerships − share expertise, tackle common challenges and reinforce our mutual efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To systematically facilitate such partnerships, I announced in last year's Budget a major initiative, the Industry Transformation Maps, or ITMs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: ITMs are integrative platforms, bringing together various stakeholders − TACs, unions and the Government −to align our efforts around a common plan to transform each sector.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will develop ITMs for 23 sectors, covering about 80% of our economy.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will keep this going at a good pace and launch the remaining 17 within FY2017.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The ITMs help us to identify key enablers, which involve different stakeholders, to transform sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the Centre of Innovation for Supply Chain Management at Republic Polytechnic works with companies to level up their capabilities6 and provides students with hands-on experience.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I said last year, the ITMs are "live" plans that we will adjust along the way.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Where we spot opportunities, including ones that do not fit any existing industry, we will adapt our ITMs to seize them.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must also maximise synergies between related ITMs, such as between the food services and hotel industries.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our companies, TACs and unions can play a key role in the success of our ITMs.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singtel has also launched its Cyber Security Institute to train technical professionals, management and boards to better handle cyber breaches.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the emphasis on innovation, Government agencies need to play enabling roles, to help realise new ideas.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our regulatory agencies must balance managing risk and creating the space to test innovations.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will give them greater flexibility, making Singapore more conducive to venture capital investment, thereby enhancing the supply of financing for startups.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can also create more space for innovation through regulatory sandboxes.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This involves setting boundaries within which some rules can be suspended, to allow greater experimentation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Likewise, MAS has set up a regulatory sandbox for financial technology.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Regulatory agencies will further explore how we can facilitate innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, our regulators can make their risk assessments for new products and services more swift and effective.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A good example is the Health Sciences Authority (HSA), which will be setting up a priority review scheme to evaluate new and innovative medical devices.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will accelerate the commercialisation process and make Singapore a preferred location to launch these devices.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also support our agencies to procure products and services in a way that builds capabilities in the economy and supports innovation.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will allow Government agencies to procure innovative and productive construction solutions, which may have higher costs as these solutions may be nascent and lack scale.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The fund will allow these solutions to enter and gain traction in the market.

speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be over and above the $4.5 billion set aside last year for the Industry Transformation Programme.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also invest in shared infrastructure for economic clusters, so that industry players can network, pool resources and share knowledge.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Last year, I spoke about how the Jurong Innovation District would be an exciting development to live, work and innovate in.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: A vibrant city must also have diverse social spaces where people can come together, create shared experiences and forge stronger bonds.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are currently working with the community to design the new Jurong Lake Gardens as our new national gardens in the heartlands.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also continue to invest in more sports and arts facilities around the island.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Beyond physical infrastructure, we are also enhancing sports and arts programmes.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will share more on these efforts later.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our vibrant and connected city must also be sustainable and resilient.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: A high-quality living environment endears the city to its residents and visitors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Around the world, the effects of climate change and air and water pollution are worsening public health and quality of life.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As an island, Singapore is vulnerable to rises in sea levels due to climate change.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Together with the international community, we have to play our part to protect our living environment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In doing so, we secure a better future not only for ourselves, but for generations to come.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is in our own interest to support the international coordination required to deal with an issue that affects all countries and, in particular, small island states like ours.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: One is to ensure consumers understand the effects of their actions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So, we have energy efficiency labels, like the ticks on air-conditioners or refrigerators.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Singapore has good environmental protection standards and the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources continues to ensure that our regulations are up to date.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: But the most economically efficient and fair way to reduce greenhouse gas emissions is to set a carbon tax, so that emitters will take the necessary actions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is in the range of what other jurisdictions have implemented.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It will create a price signal to incentivise industries to reduce their emissions, complementing the regulatory measures which we are also introducing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It will help us to achieve our commitments to reduce emissions under the Paris Agreement, do so efficiently and at as low a cost to the economy as possible.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This may also spur the creation of new opportunities in green growth industries, such as clean energy.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Revenue from the carbon tax will help to fund measures by industries to reduce emissions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The impact of the carbon tax on most businesses and households should be modest.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Government has started industry consultations and will continue to reach out.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The final carbon tax and exact implementation schedule will be decided after our consultations and further studies.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will take into consideration the lessons from other countries and prevailing economic conditions in Singapore in implementation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also provide appropriate measures to ease the transition.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Apart from carbon emissions, diesel emits highly pollutive particulate matter and nitrogen oxides which are associated with an increased risk of lung cancer and respiratory infection7.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The over-use of diesel cars has resulted in cities like London, Paris and Rome being enveloped in smog in recent years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Many of these cities have started taking action to reduce these harmful emissions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Athens, Madrid, Mexico City and Paris have announced plans to ban diesel vehicles from their city centres by 2025.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, motor fuels, such as petrol and compressed natural gas, are taxed based on how much is used.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This approach incentivises users to reduce consumption and manufacturers to develop more energy-efficient vehicles.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: However, for diesel, we levy a lump sum Special Tax on diesel cars and taxis, regardless of the amount of diesel used.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will introduce a volume-based duty at $0.10 per litre on automotive diesel, industrial diesel and the diesel component in biodiesel.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Taxing diesel according to usage incentivises users to reduce diesel consumption.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the same time, I will permanently reduce the annual Special Tax on diesel cars and taxis by $100 and $850 respectively.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In this way, we shift from an annual amount of tax to one which is related to usage.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Special Tax reduction will offset the impact of diesel duty for the majority of drivers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I strongly urge taxi companies to pass on the Special Tax reduction to taxi drivers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: There will be additional cash rebates for diesel buses ferrying school children.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For the large majority of vehicles, the first year's rebates will more than offset the diesel duty incurred in the same period.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Details of the duty changes and offset measures are in the Annex   I will also adjust two vehicle incentive schemes to encourage the use of cleaner vehicles.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: With this scheme, we hope to nudge car buyers towards cleaner and environmentally-friendly models.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the interim, we will extend the current CEVS until 31 December 20178.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also enhance and extend the Early Turnover Scheme for commercial diesel vehicles.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This scheme was first introduced in 2013 to encourage the early replacement of older and more pollutive commercial diesel vehicles.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Since then, vehicle owners have switched 27,000 vehicles to cleaner models.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Transport and the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources will share more details at the COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Water sufficiency is a matter of national survival.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Imported water and local catchment water currently meet more than half of our water demand, but both sources depend heavily on weather conditions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To meet increasing water demand and strengthen the resilience of our water supply, we have invested in desalination and NEWater plants.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These are costly but necessary investments which we must continue to make.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have priced water to reflect the higher costs of desalination and NEWater production because every additional drop of water has to come from these two sources.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The cost of water production and transmission has increased as we build more desalination and NEWater plants and lay deeper pipes through an urbanised environment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Water prices were last revised in 2000, almost 20 years ago.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As part of this exercise, we will be restructuring the Sanitary Appliance Fee and the Waterborne Fee into a single, volume-based fee.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is more reflective of the volume of used water discharged.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For 75% of households, the increase in monthly water bills will be less than $18.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will have measures to help lower- and middle-income households manage this increase.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, we impose a Water Conservation Tax on potable water to promote conservation.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To encourage the conservation of NEWater among industrial users, we will also impose a Water Conservation Tax on NEWater, which will be 10% of the NEWater tariff, starting from 1 July 2017.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The various emissions and water-related measures in Budget 2017 are necessary to protect our living environment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These will help keep our home in good shape for future generations.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is the right thing to do, even though some of these measures will lead to increases in household costs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Government will help households, especially low-income ones.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Before I speak on these household support measures, let me first speak on our measures to build a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are building an inclusive and caring society, one where Singaporeans of all backgrounds can improve their lives, where the vulnerable are uplifted and where people of all ages can look to the future with optimism.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Government will continue to support families, help the needy and catalyse community efforts.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the last decade, we have significantly increased our social spending and strengthened safety nets9.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Many Singaporeans are also stepping forward to help others in need.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our population is ageing, families are smaller and our social needs are more complex.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even as the Government strengthens direct support, more people need to help out.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In many areas, the human connection is critical − taking care of loved ones and neighbours, volunteering for worthy causes, organising community events or raising donations.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We must strengthen the gotong royong spirit where each one of us does our part to help one another.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the past two years, we enhanced parental leave10 and grants for new-borns11.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In this Budget, we will provide additional support for families, in the areas of housing, pre-school and post-secondary education.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Many couples start their lives together by applying for a Build-To-Order (BTO) flat12 which is highly subsidised.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For others, a resale flat may better meet their needs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Some may wish to live near their parents.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Some may prefer to move earlier into their own home.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To help them, we will increase subsidies for those who buy their first Housing and Development Board (HDB) home from the resale market.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for National Development will announce other measures to help young families get their first home at the COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Over the last five years, we increased childcare places by over 40%, to about 140,000.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Now, there are enough places for more than half of all children between 18 months and six years of age.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will provide more support for those with infants, that is, children under 18 months of age.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At present, about 4,000, or 8% of all infants are enrolled in centre-based infant care.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will give more details at the COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Senior Minister of State in charge of population issues at the Prime Minister's Office will also speak about our efforts to keep Singapore a Great Place for Families.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will increase annual bursary amounts for those attending Post-Secondary Education Institutions, or PSEIs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Next, we will extend PSEI bursaries to more families by revising the income eligibility criteria.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In total, PSEI bursaries will increase from about $100 million to $150 million per year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) will provide more details at the COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Earlier, I said that we would help households offset some of the increase in water prices.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will increase the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Voucher − U-Save Rebate for eligible HDB households, by an amount ranging from $40 to $120, depending on flat type, as seen in the table.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Families living in 1- and 2-room HDB flats will receive $380 of U-Save rebates each year compared to $260, while families living in 3- and 4-room HDB flats will receive $340 and $300 per year respectively, compared to $240 and $220.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Taking into account these higher U-Save rebates, 75% of all HDB households will see an average increase of less than $12 in their monthly water expenses; 1- and 2-room HDB households will, on average, have no increase in their water expenses.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will cost an additional $71 million each year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The U-Save rebate will soften the impact of the water price increase.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Even as we provide this assistance, we should not lose sight of the scarcity of water and thus should conserve it.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To help lower-income households with expenses, we will provide a one-off GST Voucher − Cash Special Payment of up to $200 for eligible GST Voucher − Cash recipients.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is in addition to the regular GST Voucher − Cash.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In total, eligible Singaporeans can receive up to $500 in cash for 2017, as seen in the table.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The one-off Special Payment will cost about $280 million and benefit more than 1.3 million Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also extend the Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) rebate and raise it by 0.5 months for FY2017.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As seen in the table, this year, we will provide 1.5 to 3.5 months of S&CC rebate to eligible HDB households; 1- and 2-room HDB households will receive a total of 3.5 months of rebates, while 3- and 4-room households will receive 2.5 months of rebates.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will cost the Government $120 million and benefit about 880,000 HDB households.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will give households a reduction in their tax bills for this year.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The rebate will cost the Government $385 million.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In total, we will provide additional support of over $850 million this year to help households with their expenses.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To support the increase in U-Save I announced earlier and other future GST Voucher payments, I will make a $1.5 billion top-up to the GST Voucher Fund.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Since the last top-up in FY2013, MediFund utilisation has increased by an average of 9% per year from FY2013 to FY2015.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will, therefore, also top up MediFund by $500 million, bringing the total fund size to $4.5 billion.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In addition, I will top up the ComCare Fund by $200 million.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This fund supports families and individuals in need.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will now speak on measures to foster a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: All of us can play a part in our communities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: All of us have something to offer, be it time, expertise or the extra attention, to care for one another.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It takes all of us to build an inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Enabling Masterplans are five-year national plans to support persons with disabilities and their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Masterplan calls for the Government and the community to better integrate persons with disabilities into the workforce and to give more support to their caregivers.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, higher-functioning graduands from Special Education schools who can work are matched to special training programmes to prepare them for employment.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will make these training programmes available to not only graduands with mild intellectual disability and autism, but also those with moderate intellectual and multiple disabilities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The centre will also work with voluntary welfare organisations (VWOs) to pilot programmes catering to caregivers of newly-diagnosed persons with disabilities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will elaborate at the COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We must also rally around those with mental health conditions, including dementia.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Mental health issues may not be easy to talk about, but we can make good progress when the community comes together.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Since 2012, the Ministry of Health (MOH) has partnered VWOs to set up 36 teams that provide outreach and allied health support in the community.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Last year, MOH also launched Dementia Friendly Communities in Hong Kah North, MacPherson and Yishun.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: These communities are networks of residents, businesses and services trained to look out for and help those with symptoms of dementia.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will resource VWOs to set up more community-based teams to support those in need, as well as educate the public on mental health issues.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: MOH will provide mental health care services in polyclinics, as part of its broader effort to improve the delivery of care within the community.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also involve the wider community and expand the number of Dementia Friendly Communities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The National Council for Social Services will also lead efforts to integrate persons with mental health issues at the workplace and in the wider society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Health will elaborate during the COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Beyond supporting families and those with greater needs, this Budget also aims to strengthen community bonds.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Since 2002, the VWOs-Charities Capability Fund has helped VWOs and charities train their staff, expand their reach and serve people better.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: So far, we have committed over $180 million of funding.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This has helped around 400 VWOs and charities.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will provide further details at the COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our Self-Help Groups have also been doing good work, working closely with the community to help needy families and children.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To enable them to do more, I will provide an additional $6 million grant to the Self-Help Groups over the next two years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: One way we bring our society together is through sports, be it playing sports with friends and neighbours, or cheering on our sportsmen and women.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Last year, we cheered our Olympic and Paralympics athletes who gave their very best and did us proud.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will do more to make it easier for all Singaporeans to participate in sports.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Over $50 million has been set aside to support community sports.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will expand the Sports-In-Precinct Programme, so that more Singaporeans can play sports near their homes.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will also expand the SportCares Programme, which encourages disadvantaged youth to discover their strengths through sports.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: To help aspiring athletes reach their full potential, we will commit an additional $50 million in grants over five years.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On top of that, we will provide up to $50 million to match sports donations dollar-for-dollar.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will build a wider base of support for Team Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth will provide more details at the COS.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Like sports, cultural activities build bonds among our people.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Increasingly, many people not only visit museums and attend performances, but also participate actively as docents and donors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Cultural Matching Fund currently provides dollar-for-dollar matching for donations to cultural institutions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Since the Fund was implemented in 2014, about $150 million has been committed, and donations to arts and heritage causes have more than doubled.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Budget 2017 is an investment in our economic transformation and social resilience.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will continue to invest in security measures to keep Singaporeans safe, and in infrastructure to support economic growth and improve quality of life.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We have been able to commit to these medium-term investments because we have a sustainable fiscal system.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Previous generations planned ahead and set aside savings when our economy was growing rapidly.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We now benefit from the returns on our Reserves.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the same time, our pro-growth and progressive tax system has given us a steady revenue stream.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Together, these have allowed us to fund new priorities without cutting back on essential areas.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the coming years, we expect expenditure needs to rise rapidly, particularly in healthcare and infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The new Changi Terminal 5 is another critical national infrastructure that will cost tens of billions of dollars.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Changi Airport is our gateway to the world.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: By enhancing our connectivity, we expand opportunities for our people.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the longer term, we must also prepare to upgrade and renew existing projects, to keep Singapore a good home.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As these infrastructure projects are costly, we have to plan ahead.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: With our spending needs increasing, the Government must continue to spend judiciously, emphasising value-for-money and drive innovation in delivery.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: For four Ministries that are serving security needs, or significantly expanding their services, namely, the Ministries of Home Affairs, Defence, Health and Transport, the 2% adjustment will be phased in over FY2017 and FY2018.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Some of the funds will be used for cross-agency projects to deliver value to citizens and businesses.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Examples include initiatives by the Municipal Services Office.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Growing our economy is the first and most important step to increasing our revenues sustainably.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We need to achieve this growth by implementing the strategies set out in the CFE.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Next, we need to strengthen our revenue base in a pro-growth and progressive manner.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Over the past five years, we have revised our tax structure as well as the Net Investment Returns framework to ensure that we have sufficient revenue for our increased spending needs till 2020.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Like all Finance Ministers before me, it is my duty to take the long view.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our domestic needs will grow over time and the global environment will shift.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We must study the implications and prepare our options early.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: One international development affecting tax systems worldwide is the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting, or BEPS, project.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The BEPS project seeks to ensure that companies are taxed where substantive economic activities are performed.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are, in consultation with businesses, refining our schemes and implementing the relevant standards.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Countries, large and small, are also reviewing their corporate tax regimes to keep them competitive.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: With increasing digital transactions and cross-border trade, some countries have taken steps to adjust their GST system to ensure a level playing field between their local businesses which are GST-registered, and foreign-based ones which are not.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We are studying how we can do likewise.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We must make these decisions in good time to ensure that our future generations remain on a sustainable fiscal footing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As the Chinese idiom goes, 未雨綢繆, let us thatch the roof before it rains.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I will extend and strengthen tax incentives to enhance our business competitiveness, such as in the financial and global trading sectors.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I shall introduce refinements to vehicle taxes for motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Today, all motorcycles incur the same Additional Registration Fee, or ARF, at 15% of their Open Market Value (OMV).

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: A small but rising number of buyers are buying expensive motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Their motorcycles have OMVs similar to those of small cars.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Just as we introduced tiers to the ARF for cars in 2013 to improve progressivity, I will introduce two more tiers for more expensive motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The ARF for motorcycles with OMV of up to $5,000 will remain at the current 15%.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The next $5,000 of motorcycle OMV will be subject to an ARF rate of 50%.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The remaining motorcycle OMV beyond $10,000 will be subject to an ARF rate of 100%.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Based on today's registration trends, we expect that more than half of new motorcycle buyers will continue to pay the current ARF rate of 15%.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The tiered ARF will apply to motorcycles registered with COEs obtained from the second February COE bidding exercise onwards.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As a complementary measure, the Ministry of Transport will cease the contribution of motorcycle COE quota to open category COE quota.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will help to address the gradual decline in motorcycle population, as very few open category COEs have been used to register motorcycles.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is higher than the surplus of $3.4 billion, or 0.8% of GDP, budgeted a year ago.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Nevertheless, when we exclude Government top-ups to funds and Net Investment Returns Contribution from Past Reserves, we expect a basic deficit of $5.6 billion, or 1.4% of GDP.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Budget 2017 outlines how we can thrive in an uncertain and rapidly changing world.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It is a call for us to pull together − the Government, firms, unions, community organisations and individuals, with everyone doing his part.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our bonds will help us to develop greater resilience in the face of unexpected shifts and improve our ability to adapt.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On the economic front, Budget 2017 sets out some support measures to address near-term concerns, particularly for sectors currently facing cyclical headwinds.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It also sets out how we will implement our medium-term economic strategies to create new opportunities and jobs.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will build capabilities in our firms and workers so that they can operate well internationally, use digital technology and innovate.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will strengthen partnerships across the economy, with the Government playing an enabling role and drawing different stakeholders together to align efforts.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: On the social front, Budget 2017 supports families who wish to buy a home, enjoy the joys of parenthood and help their children through post-secondary education.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: It also takes further steps towards building an inclusive society, for persons with disabilities and those with mental health conditions.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Just as importantly, this Budget will strengthen community bonds and partnerships among the Government, community organisations and individuals to build a better society together.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I want to take a moment here to applaud the good work done by the thousands of volunteers, working in partnership with Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Government schemes and funding can play a supporting role, but it is ultimately human relationships and community bonds that build a society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Only through concerted partnership between Government and people can we realise our vision of a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will do all this while maintaining fiscal discipline.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This will lay a sustainable foundation for future generations to thrive.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Singaporeans are chasing their dreams in various fields and are excelling on the international stage: Mathew Tham topped the Young Chef Olympiad; Ding Eu-Wen won an international design award for his smart bicycle helmet; Nathan Hartono did us proud at the Sing!

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: China competition; Nur Syahidah Alim won double gold medals in archery at the ASEAN Para Games; Yip Pin Xiu won multiple medals at the Paralympics, and Joseph Schooling, was our first Olympic gold medallist.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This strong can-do spirit will serve us well in the years ahead.
